latin: Per coelum in Epinomide, quod dicit Plato esse nobis causam omnium bonorum, non ideam coeli, sed ipsum coelum, quod est coeleste animal, intelligere debemus.
translation: When the Epinomis calls heaven the cause of all our goods, Plato does not mean the idea of heaven; he means heaven as such—the living celestial creature itself—and that is what we should understand by the term.
